title: Fall of a bound pair of two bodies in a sharp field

key_results.statement: For the sharp stationary field start, $C(\Psi\otimes\varphi)=((C_{\rm red}+e_f)\Psi)\otimes\varphi$ with $C_{\rm red}=\sum_i[A_i+\sum_xP^{(i)}_x\otimes(1+g_ix)G_i+\kappa\hat x_i\otimes X]+U$, the contract of an admissible description of $b_1,b_2,c$; a binding with a factor of the field would need a three-object term, which (1.10) does not contain.

$C_{\rm bod}=C^{\rm D}_1+C^{\rm D}_2+U+\sum_ig_i\hat x_i\otimes G_i+\kappa\langle X\rangle(\hat x_1+\hat x_2)$, fixed by $C$, $\chi$, $\varphi$ up to an additive constant; $g_1$, $g_2$, $\kappa\langle X\rangle$, as the coefficients read from $C_{\rm bod}$, are fixed by it and well defined, while the listed numbers $\gamma\theta_i$ and $\kappa\langle\chi\vert X\vert\chi\rangle$ can change under a relisting.

On the levels the gradient terms are $\hat X_\eta\mathcal K+\hat r\mathcal D_\eta$ with $\mathcal K=g_1M_1\sigma^{(1)}_3+g_2M_2\sigma^{(2)}_3+2\kappa\langle X\rangle$ independent of $\eta$ and $\mathcal D_\eta=\mathcal D_0-\eta\mathcal K$, which depends on $\eta$ unless all gradients vanish.

For every binding of $\mathcal W$, every bound level and every packet of $\mathcal G(\mathcal P_0)$, the first-order velocities of both parts are $v^{(1)}_i(\lambda)=\lambda\langle\alpha\rangle_g+\rho_i(\lambda)$ with the same coefficient, $\alpha(P)=-E_b''\langle\mathcal K\rangle_P+E_b'\partial_P\langle\mathcal K\rangle_P$.

The rest $\rho_i$ of the first-order velocity is given explicitly, with $\rho_i(0)=0$ and $\lvert\rho_i(\lambda)\rvert\le\tau_i\mathsf B_g$ for all $\lambda$, where $\mathsf B_g$ is finite because the level is isolated on the support of $g$ and $g'$ is square integrable; the rests of the two parts differ in general.

The first-order change of the mean label separation is $\lambda\langle\beta\rangle_g+\sigma(\lambda)$ with bounded $\sigma$ and $\beta=-\langle\mathcal K\rangle_P\partial_P\langle\hat r\rangle_P-2E_b'\,\mathrm{Re}\langle\hat r\psi_P\vert R_P\vert\mathcal K\psi_P\rangle$; there is no term in $\lambda^2$; $\beta\equiv0$ if $W(-r)^{*}=W(r)$ (a sufficient condition), in particular for every diagonal on-site binding; without it $\beta\not\equiv0$ in general, which rests on a numerical control only.

With the window average first and the sharp-total-label limit second, on the class $\mathcal S(P_0,I)$ of packet sequences, the drift acceleration of both parts at $P_0$ is $g_1\alpha_1(P_0)+g_2\alpha_2(P_0)+\kappa\langle X\rangle\alpha_X(P_0)$ with $\alpha_i=-M_i[E_b''\partial_{M_i}E_b-E_b'\partial_{M_i}E_b']$, $\alpha_X=-2E_b''$; the two limits do not commute on the class in general: in the other order the limit at a fixed window does not exist on the class for a window with $\mathsf f_i\neq0$ (in particular for $\partial_P\langle\mathcal K\rangle_{P_0}\neq0$) and depends on the place of the packet where it exists, while nothing is shown for $\mathsf f_i=0$, which includes $g_1=g_2=0$ and every diagonal on-site binding at $P_0=0$.

For the common gradient the coefficient is $-E_b''\mathcal M_P+E_b'\mathcal M_P'$ with $\mathcal M_P=M_1\langle\sigma^{(1)}_3\rangle_P+M_2\langle\sigma^{(2)}_3\rangle_P=E_b-\langle A_1\rangle_P-\langle A_2\rangle_P-\langle U\rangle_P$: only the rest terms of the scaling relation enter.

For a diagonal on-site binding with $\hat w_{11}\neq0$, at leading order in $\mathsf R$ and fixed $u$, the drift acceleration of the pair from rest is $a_{\rm pair}=\frac{\varsigma}{\sqrt{1+u^2}}\frac{g_1M_1+g_2M_2+2\kappa\langle X\rangle}{\mathfrak m_1+\mathfrak m_2}$, with a relative remainder $O(\epsilon^2)$ on each of the three coefficients that is not uniform in $u$; at leading order it is $-\varsigma(1+u^2)^{-1/2}$ times the inertia-weighted mean $\bar a$ of the free falls.

Ordered limits of the leading coefficient (first $\epsilon\to0$ at fixed $u$): $a_{\rm pair}\to-\varsigma\bar a[1-u^2/2+O(u^4)]$ for $u\to0$ and $a_{\rm pair}\to-\varsigma(\bar a/u)[1+O(u^{-2})]\to0$ for $u\to\infty$.

open_issues: The second order in the gradients and the range of λ over which the first order describes the motion are not estimated; (13.9) and (13.10) bound first-order terms only.

Outside the scope of the question (item 2(c) as amended): the evaluation of the limits in the other order, with the sharp total label first. Not decided here: whether that order exists for the exceptional members of Step 5.3 (f_i = 0), among them the levels of items 3 and 4 at P0 = 0.
A binding of the class W with β not identically zero is exhibited numerically (set S5), not analytically.
The relative remainders O(ε²) of (13.13)–(13.20) are not determined (numerically up to 4 % at τ/M = 0.2) and are not uniform in u.
The first-order corrections to the clock reading of a pair in the field (the gradient across the packet) are not derived.
The results hold for a binding and for motion terms without a factor of the field; whether another admissible coupling makes the pair fall like its parts is outside this package.

The remainder of (13.22) rests on the reading of the quoted statement of 11-bound-pair given in Step 7.2 (a complex neighbourhood of the real data, M1 and M2 included, whose size does not depend on ε); the statement is worded for the differentiation that gives (11.14), and the second derivatives in M1, M2 follow from its premise, not from its wording; the numerical check finds the order ε⁴ for three sets.

consistency_checks.check: One body and no binding: (13.8) applied to one free body reproduces (4.7) with g_ζ = 0 for all p and both branches; the ordered limit u → 0 with w11 < 0 of (13.13) is the inertia-weighted mean of the free falls.
Common gradient against the scaling relation (11.6): with (11.14) at P = 0 both sides of (13.12) equal M1 + M2 − aΛ.
